stem: A 55-year-old woman has recurrent kidney stones and a year of aching bones. Calcium is 12.1 mg/dL, phosphate is low, alkaline phosphatase is raised and parathyroid hormone is high. Skeletal radiographs are taken.
oneliner: 55F + kidney stones + bone pain + Ca 12.1, low phosphate, high ALP and PTH → which radiograph finding?
ask: Which radiograph finding is most likely?

options.A: Subperiosteal erosions on the radial side of middle phalanges
options.B: Coarse trabeculae with thick cortex and enlarged bones
options.D: Punched-out lytic skull lesions without sclerosis

whyNot.B: Enlarged, coarse bone: **Paget disease**, where calcium and PTH stay normal, not **high calcium with high PTH**
whyNot.C: Metaphyseal fraying: **rickets** at open growth plates in children, with low or normal calcium; she is 55 with **high calcium**
whyNot.D: Punched-out lytic lesions: **multiple myeloma**, where high calcium suppresses PTH; her **PTH is high**
whyNot.E: Joint-margin erosions: **rheumatoid arthritis**, which does not raise **calcium or PTH**

answer: Subperiosteal bone resorption of the phalanges (osteitis fibrosa cystica)
why: **High calcium with high PTH** is primary hyperparathyroidism. Long-standing excess PTH stimulates osteoclasts, giving **subperiosteal resorption**, classically along the **radial side of the middle phalanges**, plus osteopenia and brown tumors.

idea.rule: Primary hyperparathyroidism erodes bone from under the periosteum, most visibly on the radial side of the middle phalanges.
also: Brown tumors are cystic hemosiderin-rich osteoclast masses
Raised alkaline phosphatase reflects osteoblast activity

stem: A 35-year-old woman has a firm thyroid nodule. Serum calcitonin is high, and her father had an adrenal tumor that caused episodic hypertension. A biopsy of the nodule is examined under the microscope.
oneliner: 35F + thyroid nodule + high calcitonin + father with pheochromocytoma → which biopsy finding?
ask: Which biopsy finding is most likely?

options.A: Papillae with Orphan Annie eye nuclei and psammoma bodies
options.B: Nests of polygonal cells in amyloid-rich stroma
options.C: Follicles with capsular and vascular invasion
options.D: Lymphoid follicles with germinal centers and Hurthle cells
options.E: Granulomas with multinucleated giant cells around colloid

whyNot.A: Papillae with clear, overlapping nuclei and calcified round bodies: **papillary carcinoma**, with normal calcitonin
whyNot.C: Neoplastic follicles that break through the capsule or blood vessels: **follicular carcinoma**, with normal calcitonin
whyNot.D: Lymphoid follicles with germinal centers: **Hashimoto thyroiditis**, with high TSH rather than a nodule with calcitonin
whyNot.E: Granulomas with giant cells around colloid: **subacute granulomatous thyroiditis**, painful with a raised ESR

answer: Polygonal C-cell nests in amyloid stroma (medullary carcinoma)
why: **High calcitonin** with a family history of **pheochromocytoma** points to medullary thyroid carcinoma of **parafollicular C cells**. Tumor cells form nests in a pink **amyloid stroma** made from calcitonin, often with surrounding C-cell hyperplasia.

idea.rule: Medullary thyroid carcinoma: C-cell nests in calcitonin-derived amyloid, stained by Congo red.
also: Amyloid shows apple-green birefringence under polarized light
MEN2A and MEN2B are RET mutations
C cells arise from neural crest

stem: A 45-year-old woman has fatigue, constipation and a painless, firm, diffusely enlarged thyroid. TSH is high, free T4 is low and anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies are present. A biopsy of the gland is examined under the microscope.
oneliner: 45F + fatigue, painless firm goiter + high TSH, low free T4 + anti-TPO antibodies → which biopsy finding?
ask: Which biopsy finding is most likely?

options.B: Tall crowded follicular cells with scalloped colloid
options.C: Dense fibrosis extending into neck muscles
options.D: Lymphoid follicles with germinal centers and Hurthle cells

whyNot.A: Granulomas with giant cells: **subacute thyroiditis**, painful with a raised ESR and early thyrotoxicosis
whyNot.B: Tall, crowded follicular cells with scalloped colloid: **Graves disease**, with low TSH
whyNot.C: Fibrosis invading neck muscles: **Riedel thyroiditis**, a rock-hard fixed gland; hers is **diffusely enlarged** with **anti-TPO**, the Hashimoto pattern
whyNot.E: Spindle cells in amyloid stroma: **medullary carcinoma**, with high calcitonin

answer: Lymphoid follicles with germinal centers (Hashimoto thyroiditis)
why: A painless goiter with **hypothyroidism** and **anti-TPO antibodies** is Hashimoto thyroiditis. The gland is packed with **lymphocytes forming germinal centers**, and the follicular cells show **Hurthle (oncocytic) change**.

idea.rule: Hashimoto thyroiditis: lymphoid follicles with germinal centers and Hurthle cells.
also: Risk of primary thyroid B-cell lymphoma is raised
